lines.en: label dormwarsfive8:
scene courtroomcontest1
: For the honorable judge Imani Imai to preside over the case of Kumon-mi vs. Wakana Watabe!
scene courtroomcontest2
: You may now be seated.
: Ya didn’t give any of us chairs!
: That’s not true...the jury and...the lawyers have them...
: Oh, so the common man gets screwed over again! Typical justice system!
: Damn it. Starting to think I should’ve appointed a bailiff if y’all are just gonna be talking the whole time.
scene courtroomcontest3
: Regardless! Today’s trial will serve to determine whether or not one Wakana Watabe is guilty of crimes against humanity. Specifically that of the custodial variety.
: Three more janitors were found dead last week. And Kumon-mi’s district attorney, Makoto Miyamura, believes our lovable goth teacher lady is responsible!
: Is “lovable” really the word we’re using to describe Miss Watabe now? Isn’t her entire class afraid of her?
: That just means I’m doing a good job.
scene courtroomcontest4
: Objection! Silence in the court!
: Miss Imai, it’s the attorneys who call for objection. The judge is supposed to-
scene courtroomcontest5
: Objection! Badgering the judge! You trying to get on my bad side, Miyamura?!
: Hah...no, your honor. Please excuse my outburst.
: That’s what I thought!
scene courtroomcontest6
: Now, prepare your opening statement! I ain’t got all day for this.
: Is it just me or is the judge calling the defendant “lovable” grounds for a mistrial on the case of personal bias?
: Is it just me or is there even more bias residing within the jury itself when Ayane is responsible for the deaths of at least ten janitors?
: It is my belief that this just makes me an expert on the subject, Touka. Who would be better at spotting a janitor-killer than one who has killed janitors?
: How are you so evil to the men and women who serve as the backbone of our school, but so nice to basically everyone else?
: It’s not like I try to kill them, Noriko. I’ve been acquitted every time.
: Is that not because you’re wealthy?
: It might be. Who’s to say?
: Miss Imai, may I ask a question?
: No! That’s not how this works! You speak when spoken to in this court room! You hear me, Fukuyama?!
: Yes, and quite clearly. You don’t have to yell.
: Sorry. I love you. Miyamura! Please address the jury! Timer starts now!
scene courtroomcontest7
: Timer? They’re being timed for this?
: Everyone knows the fairest court cases are those conducted under harsh time constraints with little to no prep-work done.
: You say that now, but it looks like Makoto is more than prepared for this.
: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury — first and foremost, I’d like to thank you for your time.
: As a Dorm Wars contestant myself, I personally understand just how difficult it is to step away from the festivities over such a serious matter when you should be out having fun.
scene courtroomcontest8
: That raises the question, though — with such a well-known and beloved event on the cusp of arrival, what sort of person would commit such a heinous act?
: An act that would be all but certain to disrupt such an event as it took place within these hallowed halls?
: Ladies and gentlemen, on the night of March 1st, three janitors- no. Three patriots were murdered in cold blood just two doors down from Wakana Watabe’s office.
: Objection! Speculation! We don’t know that the janitors were patriots! They might have been really bad people!
: Overruled! Anyone who cleans toilets is a patriot in my book! Continue, Miyamura.
scene courtroomcontest9
: Thank you, your honor. And let me say — it is not my goal to dredge up the respective characters of the deceased, no.
: I merely wish to bring justice to their families. And to hold the one responsible for their deaths accountable on behalf of this great city.
scene courtroomcontest10
: Which is precisely why I will prove without a shadow of a doubt that Wakana Watabe is guilty on all three counts of murder in the first degree!
: And the reason for her actions, you ask?!
scene courtroomcontest11
: To delay, or even worse — to cancel the Dorm Wars!
: Tch. She’s good.
: Just leave all the talking to me, Ms. Watabe. I’ve got it under control.
: Good. For that is your purpose as my attorney.
: And a purpose I shall fulfill...since it’s time to show this prosecutor how it’s done.
: Uta Ushibori! Please issue your opening statement to the court!
scene courtroomcontest12
: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury!
: No!
: What?
: Ushibori! Are you admitting that your client is responsible for the murder of the three janitors?!
: Quite the contrary, Miss Imai! Wakana Watabe would never even consider an act as heinous as murder.
: Which is why I find the purpose of an opening statement rather pointless. Especially when Makoto’s gonna be a big smartypants about it.
: Objection! Argumentative!
: Nuh-uh!
: Objection sustained. Uta Ushibori, the court orders you to provide an opening statement because it’s a part of the competition.
scene courtroomcontest13
: Tch. Fine. But you’ll all see within a matter of seconds that asking for one is rather pointless when the truth is as plain as day!
scene courtroomcontest14
: Wakana Watabe does not have the energy to murder anyone! She barely has the energy to get out of her chair!
: Do you really believe a woman like that is capable of murder?!
: Objection! Lack of foundation, your honor.
scene courtroomcontest15
: Shut up! You think you’re such a good lawyer just because you know stuff about being a lawyer?! As if!
: Miyamura, elaborate.
: Your honor, the defense fails to provide any factual evidence supporting the claim that Miss Watabe lacks energy when she could merely be acting tired.
: Overruled. She called me over to her apartment once just to tie her shoes since she didn’t want to bend down.
: And you came. Because you knew I wouldn’t murder you.
scene courtroomcontest16
: Objection! I told my client to let me do the talking and now she suddenly isn’t! There are probably rules against that.
: Overruled! The defendant is a strong, independent woman and is allowed to speak if she wants to!
scene courtroomcontest17
: But-
: Order in the court! I don’t have a gavel though, so just pretend I’m banging it right now.
: My, this is just like the daytime television programming I used to watch with my mother when I was younger. Just without all of the poverty.
: What do you think the chances are of them actually being able to provide any sort of evidence in a clearly fictional case?
: Evidence seldom matters at all if a lawyer is good enough at manipulating the jury. And I imagine that’s the card Uta’s going to play based on her experience with people.
scene courtroomcontest18
: You mean at the maid cafe? You think she’s going to try and manipulate us the way she does her customers?
: I don’t have any evidence to support that claim. And I may be biased as well given that Makoto is a resident of our floor. But that’s what I would do if I was her.
: Do you watch courtroom TV too, Futaba? You’ve seemed pretty engrossed in all of this since the moment we sat down.
: Not really. Rin and I used to play Ace Attorney together in middle school, though. It’s likely just residual interest from that.
: What is this “Ace Attorney” you speak of? Some type of role playing game similar to the one we saw in the cafeteria earlier?
scene courtroomcontest19
: It’s a video game series...where you...solve silly court cases and...stuff like that.
: It’s also the virtual home of Miles Edgeworth — who may or may not be the first cartoon character I ever had a crush on.
scene courtroomcontest20
: Mine was Mordecai from the Regular Show. I never had any idea what he was saying because I don’t speak English, but that voice just does it for me.
: I liked Edward from Full Metal Alchemist.
: I don’t know literally any of these things.
scene courtroomcontest21
: Did you never watch cartoons growing up, Touka?
: Animated television? Not that I can remember. I was taught that sort of content can rot one’s brain. It’s the same reason I avoid the Internet.
: That’s fair and you should probably keep it that way.
: Yeah, probably. You’re missing out on a lot of hot cartoon characters, though. And an entire genre of porn.
: Interesting. I’m learning about all sorts of interesting fetishes lately. This is the first I’m hearing of people being attracted to cartoons, though.
: Oh, it’s super common! And not at all weird. Even if it’s for something that sounds weird. Like ponies.
scene courtroomcontest22
: Ponies?...
: Yup! Not weird at all. Right, girls? Sana is wrong.
: I’m just happy that you’re happy, Noriko.
: Huh...yes, I do believe it’s good that I was kept away from animated media in hindsight.
: Oh, right. Court is in session. We should probably be paying attention to that.
scene courtroomcontest23
: ...which is why I can’t help but be appalled, your honor! Nineteen children are without a parent now!
: That’s close to the same amount of parents missing from girls in our class when assuming that the ones we know very little about, like Maya and Yasu, are missing at least one!
: Objection! Irrelevant! But also very sad!
: Sustained! And also very sad!
scene courtroomcontest24
: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, the fact remains that the bodies of all three deceased were found just several steps from Miss Watabe’s door!
: And if the discovery period was longer than ten hours, I’d be able to show you sufficient proof that their DNA was found in her office.
: Objection! Something else probably! I don’t know what it’s called, though!
: Sustained, probably! All I know is that it ain’t real evidence if it hasn’t gone through that discovery thing!
: Which I understand! But when all other roads lead back to her, you must begin to question her involvement!
: If she is not the murderer herself, which is highly unlikely based on the evidence the city of Kumon-mi has gathered, she is, at bare minimum, an accomplice.
scene courtroomcontest25
: Your honor — the defense would like to move to cross-examination as the prosecutor herself now acknowledges the possibility that my client is innocent.

: Should we take her words at face value, we can make the astute observation that this argument is built upon nothing but emotion and the desire to scapegoat my client for something she just happened to be nearby for.
: Why did you wait until now to start sounding smart? Miyamura has been wiping the floor with you so far.
scene courtroomcontest26
: Objection! Favoritism, your honor! My client clearly likes Makoto more than me!
: Overruled. The defense cannot object to itself. The court will now move to cross-examination and asks the prosecution to call upon its first witness.
: There are witnesses?! Why didn’t anyone inform me of this?!
: Your honor, the prosecution asks that one Akira Arakawa takes the stand.
: Oh, okay. Well, I guess I don’t have to worry about who knows my name and who doesn’t anymore.
scene courtroomcontest27
: Mr. Arakawa — you would consider yourself friends with Wakana Watabe, would you not?
: We’re just coworkers, really.
: Fuck you, Arakawa. I’ll kill you too.
scene courtroomcontest28
: O-Objection! The defense asks for Miss Watabe’s most recent outburst to be stricken from the record!
: Sustained! We don’t have a stenographer, so there isn’t a record! Here’s hoping the jury was paying attention!
: Hm? What? Are we voting now?
: Did Miss Watabe just admit to being guilty?
: She might have. She doesn’t look very guilty, though.
scene courtroomcontest29
: Miss Watabe! Your attorney advises you keep your mouth shut unless it’s to preach your innocence!
: Miyamura had the whole case figured out the moment she said this was done to have the Dorm Wars canceled.
: If I had known it would only make me more involved, I would have just killed myself instead.
: Objection! The Dorm Wars is fun!
scene courtroomcontest30
: Are you objecting to me?! You useless attorney! Call for a recess and negotiate a plea deal!
: Your honor! The defense asks that the prosecution continue its cross examination!
: So...no recess?
: No! I want to ask Sensei stuff too! This is fun!
scene courtroomcontest31
: Anyway, as I was saying, you’re friends with Wakana Watabe. Which means you know her better than most, correct?
: She cried into my shoulder once and it was really cute. She also smells nice and has a great body. It just doesn’t work very well.
: Don’t fucking tell them that I cried, Arakawa! I can’t look weak in front of these miscreants!
: And while Miss Watabe was crying into your shoulder, did she by any chance confess to the murder of three individuals?
: Uhh...not that I can recall.
scene courtroomcontest32
: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, take special note of that wording. “Not that I can recall.”
scene courtroomcontest31
: You acknowledge that your memory is worse than most, correct?
: That’s...right.
: So it’s possible Miss Watabe did confess her crimes to you and you just...don’t remember. Correct?
: I...guess that’s technically correct. Sure.
: And what do you think it would take to...jog your memory? A photo? A video?
: The promise for one to destroy a pre-filled marriage contract that may or may not be hidden away in a safe somewhere?
scene courtroomcontest33
: You know, it’s starting to come back to me-
: No it’s not! And it’s the defense’s turn now!
scene courtroomcontest34
: Akira Arakawa — on a scale of one to ten, how cute do you think I am?
: Ten.
: Objection! Relevance, your honor. This line of questioning has nothing to do with the case. The defense is clearly leading the witness and-
: Overruled! You’ve objected too many times!
: There’s a limit?!
: And do you believe I’ll make a great wife one day?
: You definitely seem built for that, yeah.
: And assuming we were both legal consenting adults, would you have any issue taking my hand in marriage?
: I mean...that’s a complicated-
: Just a yes or no is fine, thank you.
: Then...yes?
scene courtroomcontest35
: Your honor, this witness is clearly biased and involved in a conflict of interest. The defense calls for him to be expelled from the stand so the court can move to recess.
: Oh, you bitch.
scene courtroomcontest36
: Interesting strategy.
scene courtroomcontest37
: Unfortunately though, it appears as if the jury is already prepared to provide a verdict and that we don’t need to dismiss the court at all.
scene courtroomcontest38
: What?! No!
: Foreperson Fukuyama! How does the jury find the defendant?!
: In the case of the city of Kumon-mi vs Wakana Watabe — we, the jury, find the defendant to be guilty on all three counts of murder in the first degree.
: On what grounds?!
: On the grounds that she confessed to being guilty on all three counts of murder in the first degree.
: Gah! All you had to do was keep your mouth shut, Miss Watabe!
: No, you still probably would have lost either way.
scene courtroomcontest39
: The court rules in favor of Kumon-mi and sentences Wakana Watabe to a $100 fine payable in either food or alcohol at her earliest convenience.
: Three counts of murder and all she gets is a $100 fine?
: I’m tellin’ you guys! The system’s broken! They don’t care about the common man! We want justice for the families of those three janitors!
: Fine. The charge is increased to $300 effective immediately. Court is now adjourned.
scene black
: Boom! Justice achieved! This is why ya rise up, girls.
: I don’t know...I still feel like the charge is a little light.
scene courtroomcontest40
: You know, ignoring the fact that Wakana basically just got away with murder, that went a lot better than I would have expected after hearing about a mock court case in school.
: Makocchi was great. I probably should’ve taken it a little more seriously, though.
scene courtroomcontest41
: Makocchi?
: Your nickname!
: Interesting. I’m not used to nicknames that aren’t inherently hurtful.
: What’s the plan now? Why are you two just waiting around out here? Looks like everybody else went home already.
scene courtroomcontest42
: Nobody went home! They’re all heading over to Koi Cafe for the next tournament.
: Which is...what exactly?
: Another stand-up comedy showdown. Which is why we wouldn’t hold it against you if you didn’t want to come since the last one got really weird.
: But if you did want to come, we’d be happy if you walked there with us! And if you stay in the center, you can hold both of our hands at once!
: Who is...competing exactly?
: Not Tsuneyo if that’s what you’re worried about.
: It’s Futaba and Touka this time — two of the least controversial girls we have! Who are, somewhat coincidentally, probably not going to be very funny.
: Which is why we think you should come with us. And praise us both along the way for how exceptional and smart we were just now.
: Just think, Sensei! How many more opportunities will you ever have to praise me for being smart?
: You guys don’t need to convince me. I’ll join you. I could use some coffee after all of today’s...excitement anyway.
: Are you happy to be back? Wanna come out of retirement and give Makoto somebody to follow around like a puppy again?
: I’d say she’s more of an overly-obedient service dog than a puppy. Which I assumed Imani was getting to experience now in place of me.
: Imani’s actually good at her job, so she doesn’t need as much help.
: I figured. Which is why it’s weird that you two want me back at all.
: There’s nothing weird about wanting to spend more time with the boy you like. Right, Makoto?
: Exactly. And I think it’s fine to let my grades suffer a little bit given the circumstances of everything. Right, Sensei?
: So you two just...you’re openly competing now?
scene courtroomcontest43
: Most of us are, yeah.
: The majority of the class has accepted by now that we’re active participants in a perpetual battle for your heart.
: So some of us are forming alliances while others are contacting the black market to find out which organs sell for the most money.
: Hearts go for about a million US dollars — which is fun because they’re also the most poetic organ to harvest when fighting a battle for someone’s love.
: Please don’t make this a thing that just...everyone’s okay with.
scene courtroomcontest44
: We hide it from the other teachers if that’s what you’re worried about.
: Though, I’ll be the first to admit that things do become a little obvious with Miss Imai around sometimes. We should probably hide that better.
: You should hide it from each other too.
: I don’t want any of you ruining your relationships over someone like me when I never should have dragged you into my life in the first place.
: Probably not. But we’re glad that you did.
: You think I’d wear a skirt this tight for just anybody?
: Don’t actually answer that question. It’ll only hurt my feelings.
: ...I’ll walk with you guys.
scene black
: I just ask that you don’t make this feel normal for me.
: It’s not the same if I have nothing to fear.
